//: MERGE every TOP-LEVEL key of this file into ~/.claude/settings.json (worktree is a sibling of hooks, NOT inside it) — never replace existing keys. Keep any PreToolUse entry already there (a delete-confinement guard, say) and ADD the entries below beside it. The worktree key lets fresh worktrees (implementer/verifier isolation) reach their dependencies through symlinks; add whatever directory names your repos use. The SessionStart entry runs session-engines.sh, which announces the active engine map; its matcher limits it to startup, resume and clear — compaction is covered by the PostCompact entry, which re-injects the policy. TIMEOUT BUDGET — the commit gate's timeout of 600 below is the budget a repo's make check must fit inside. A PreToolUse hook that times out does NOT block the tool, so a check that overran used to leave every commit ungated while looking gated, with no error to read. check-gate.sh now closes that hole itself: it reads this timeout from your settings, stops the checks 30 seconds before it, and BLOCKS the commit with a message when they did not finish — a loud refusal in place of a silent allow. dod.sh does the same against the Stop entry's timeout. Raising the number therefore no longer opens a hole; it only means a commit may wait that long. Even so, a check that needs the whole budget belongs in make test — keep check the fast lane. This note lives at the TOP LEVEL and never inside a hook entry: Claude Code does not accept comments in a settings file, unknown-key tolerance inside a hook object is undocumented, and a schema validation error rejects the WHOLE settings file — every hook, permission and setting with it. After merging, run /hooks and confirm the commit gate is listed. Push is deliberately NOT gated here: whether push deploys is a fact about a repo, not about the machine, so a repo where it does adds permissions.ask with Bash(git push*) to its own .claude/settings.json.
